Folded as the DIAGNOSTIC extension of the in-build revocation-linearization layer — when a refinement check fails, RFD-1 classifies why.
intelligence.essence: Refinement Failure Attribution Law: a failed refinement check must be decomposed into independently testable obligations — abstract-model adequacy, state and transition mapping, concrete commit ordering, external assumptions, and observation completeness. No fault classification may be promoted without sufficient independent evidence. Multiple established defects must remain distinguishable, and uncertainty must not be converted into blame. The ultimate acceptance criterion: NayaNET should identify not just that its formal model and runtime disagree, but precisely where they disagree, whether the model or runtime is wrong, what evidence proves that diagnosis, and what smallest governed repair restores the guarantee — without weakening the law or discarding unaffected intelligence. A failed check proves the relationship is unestablished, not that any component is defective. Arbitrary remapping to make a history pass and weakening the model until unsafe executions become legal are both forbidden.
intelligence.falsifier: A classification promoted without independent evidence; a single forced label on a multi-cause failure; uncertainty converted into blame; the original history overwritten by the diagnosis; a repair candidate auto-flipping the diagnosis to VERIFIED; the mapping revised without semantic justification; the model weakened until a known unsafe execution passes; the law itself revised as a diagnostic shortcut.

human_view.meaning: When the proof fails, don't point fingers — do forensics. A failed refinement check means the model and the real system disagree, but it doesn't tell you who's wrong. Maybe the model forgot a legitimate state. Maybe the mapping called a dispatch a commit. Maybe the database really did commit something it shouldn't have. Maybe we assumed an outside service would enforce something it never promised. Or maybe the logs just can't tell us. The discipline: locate the FIRST point where things provably diverge, test each suspect with a discriminating experiment, keep every established cause visible instead of forcing one label, and never let uncertainty turn into blame. And the trap to avoid at all costs: 'fixing' the failure by quietly rewriting the rules until the test passes. The law is fixed. If the law needs changing, that's a separate decision — never a diagnostic shortcut. Even our own operations follow this: the rate-limit explanation for those two red jobs is a reported diagnosis, not a proven one.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the forensics layer the verification triad was missing: RLQ-1 proves the model, RLQ-MUT-1 qualifies the checker, RLQ-Refinement maps the system, RFD-1 diagnoses the disagreement. The permanent contributions: the five-class taxonomy with non-exclusivity, the first-divergence procedure, the forbidden repairs (no remap-to-pass, no weaken-to-pass), and the discipline applied reflexively to our own operations. Every future failed check inherits this shape: preserve the history, test competing explanations, classify only on evidence, repair the smallest governed thing.

intelligence.measurement_contract: RFD-1 qualification: four controlled diagnostic fixtures with sealed causes (bad abstraction, incorrect mapping, real transaction-ordering violation, unsupported external guarantee), blind diagnosis by a worker without the answer key, independent verifier comparing classifications to sealed causes; then mixed-cause and observability-gap fixtures; uncertainty preserved when key evidence is withheld. Diagnostic harness fixtures F1–F8: F7 must catch over-restrictive false rejection, F8 must be stable under irrelevant log reordering. Every diagnosis retains the four objects (history → obligation → diagnosis → repair) with the original history intact. No classification promoted without sufficient independent evidence.

naya_view.directive: Diagnose the first independently established divergence, never the first suspicious timestamp. Compare actual operation semantics, never event labels (DISPATCHED ≠ ACCEPTED ≠ COMMITTED ≠ EFFECT_OBSERVED). Report primary, contributing, and unresolved classifications separately. Preserve the original counterexample. Gate every classification through independent falsification. Test the diagnostic mechanism itself with planted defects of known cause. Never rewrite the proof standard to pass a check; the law is fixed independently of the implementation under investigation.

simple_view.meaning: When the proof fails, find the exact first point of disagreement — model, mapping, database, outside service, or just missing evidence — and never weaken the rules to make the failure go away.
